No associated meniscal tear. Mild proximal MCL sprain.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain
Comparison: Radiograph [DATE]

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: No meniscal tear or extrusion. Mild intrasubstance degeneration of the posterior horn.
Medial compartment cartilage: Mild loss of cartilage along the weightbearing aspect of the mediofemoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Mild loss of cartilage along the lateral femoral condyle.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Small partial-thickness cartilage defect along the lateral patellar facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Intact.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal. 
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Increased tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 19 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Imaged tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear. There is mild edema deep to the sartorius and gracilis tendons at the level of the knee joint which may represent bursitis.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. Mild compartmental knee osteoarthritis.
2. Intrasubstance degeneration of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus without evidence of tear.
3. Mild nonspecific edema deep to the sartorius and gracilis tendons may represent mild bursitis at the level of the knee joint.

INDICATION:     [IDENTIFIER]

IMPRESSION:  Probable bone contusion involving the lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau without discrete fracture line. Possible associated cortical/cartilaginous disruption along the lateral aspect of the intercondylar notch. Longitudinal tear of the posterior horn medial meniscus.

TECHNIQUE: MR imaging of the right knee was performed without intravenous contrast material.     

FINDINGS:

The ACL and PCL are intact.

In the medial compartment, there is a longitudinal tear of the anterior third of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus (images 6 through 8, series 4). The meniscus otherwise appears intact. There is no cartilaginous thinning or subchondral edema. The medial collateral ligament is intact.

In the lateral compartment, the lateral meniscus is intact. There is subchondral edema involving the lateral aspect of the lateral femoral condyle. There is no discrete fracture line. There is minimal edema in the adjacent lateral tibial plateau. There is no evidence of cartilaginous defect in the lateral compartment. The lateral collateral ligament is intact. 

In the patellofemoral compartment, the extensor mechanism is intact. Adjacent to the marrow edema in the lateral femoral condyle, there is the suggestion of disruption of the normal T2 hypointense cortical line along the lateral aspect of the intercondylar notch, best seen on image 22 of series 3, with possible defect in the adjacent articular cartilage (images 21 and 22, series 3). The retinacula appear within normal limits.

A physiologic amount of joint fluid is present. There is edema in the soft tissues just superficial to the lateral femoral condyle, suggesting contusion. No other periarticular soft tissue abnormalities are seen.

MRI of Left Knee with 
-SG PD FatSat, Locator, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS

* Shallow trochlear groove with supratrochlear spur and lateral displacement of patella, indicative of trochlear dysplasia with suspicious of lateral patellar tilting.
   Increased signal intensity of the medial and lateral patellar retinaculum with surrounding soft tissue edema, in favor of grade 2 injury.
   Bone marrow edema over medial aspect of patella and lateral aspect of lateral femoral condyle, R/O bone contusion.
* Wearing of the articular cartilage of patellofemoral joint and spur formation of patella, femur and anterior tibial plateau with subchondral bone marrow edema, reflecting osteoarthritis; subchondral cystic change over tibial plateau.
* There is linear signal intensity in anterior horn of lateral meniscus and posterior horn of medial meniscus, without significant extends into the surface, R/O grade 2 intrasubstance signal, maybe due to degeneration.
* High signal intensity in the soft tissues around the medial and lateral collateral ligaments and ACL, in favor of grade 1 injury.
* Joint effusion with suprapatellar expension and hypertrophy of the synovium; suprapatellar, medial and lateral plicae can also be noted, indicative of synovitis.
* Subcutaneous edema around left knee; increased fat stranding over infrapatellar fat pad.
* Mild muscle edema over vastus medialis muscle.
> The contour of PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> No evidence of tear is noted in  lateral meniscus in this study.
> The quadriceps and patellar tendons appear to be within normal.

Impression:
1. Transient patellar dislocation with tear of medial patellar retinaculum near patellar attachment and bone contusion of medial aspect of patella and lateral femoral condyle.
2. Trochlear dysplasia with shallow femoral trochlear groove and in favor of lateral patellar tilting in this study.
3. Grade 1 injury of ACL, MCL and  LCL.
4. Subcutaneous and interstitial edema around left knee and muscle edema over vastus medialis muscle.
5. Osteoarthritis of left knee with synovitis and patellar plicae.
6. R/O grade 2 intrasubstance signal in anterior horn of lateral meniscus and posterior horn of medial meniscus.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation.

Focal high-grade chondropathy in the weightbearing portion of the medial femoral condyle with minor underlying bone stress changes. Well-maintained lateral tibiofemoral and patellofemoral compartment hyaline articular cartilage.  
Conclusion:  Focal high-grade chondropathy in the weightbearing portion of the medial femoral condyle with minor underlying bone stress changes. Minimal insertional tendinosis of the quadriceps tendon at the superior pole of the patella. Ancillary findings described above.

Diz eklemi içi sıvı miktarı minimal artmış. Diz eklemindeki trikompartmantal hafif dereceli osteoartrit patellofemoral eklemde belirgin olup patella apeksi/medyal fasetindeki segmenter tam kat kondral kayıp eşlik eden subkortikal medüller fibrovasküler değişiklikler, medyal femoral kondilin ağırlık taşıyan yüzündeki fokal tam kat milimetrik kondral kayıp ve milimetrik marjinal osteofitler ile karakterize. Lateral menisküs normal. Medyal menisküs gövdesi düzeyindeki dejenerasyona arka boynuzu/gövdesi bileşkesindeki milimetrik radyal yırtık eşlik ediyor. Diz ekleminin posteromedyali ödemli olup posterior oblik-oblik popliteyal bağlardaki kalınlaşma ve intensite artışı ile birlikte. Kuadriseps yağ yastıkçığındaki hafif dereceli ödem ön diz ağrısı nedeni olabilir. Kemiklerdeki subkortikal milimetrik boyutlu T2 intensite artışları osteopeniyi telkin ediyor. Kemiklerin medülla intensiteleri bunların dışında normal. İç yan bağın çevresi ödemli. Dış yan bağ, çapraz bağlar normal. Diz eklemi çevresindeki kas yapılar atrofik. Prepatellar ve yüzeyel infrapatellar derin cilt altı bağ dokusu ödemli. Medyal gastroknemyusun origosu düzeyindeki intensite artışı tendonozisi ile uyumlu. Ekstensör mekanizma korunmuş. Proksimal tibyofibular eklem normal.
